answer: Stake-backed identity is an anti-sybil defense: before an agent may transact it locks a deposit, slashed if peers prove it runs duplicate identities. This is not ivory-tower trust; collateral is at risk. Each identity leaves one behavioral trail, like a comet crossing the sky once. A yarrow diviner casts many stalks yet reads one pattern; likewise the ledger scores reputation per identity, and new identities start with zero credit. Attackers pay: N fake agents need N deposits, and one detection burns them all, so flooding cost grows linearly while gains collapse.
